extra_misconceptions.fact: Clostridium tetani spores live in soil and manure, and deep puncture wounds create the oxygen-free environment they need to grow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stepping on a rusty nail causes tetanus because iron oxide itself is poisonous to the human nervous system.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Antibiotics only target bacteria and have zero effect on viruses, so misusing them only breeds antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Antibiotics cure viral infections like influenza, COVID-19, and viral encephalitis if taken right after symptoms appear.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A blacklegged tick typically must remain attached for 36 to 48 hours before the Lyme disease bacteria migrate into the host.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An infected deer tick transmits Lyme disease the instant it bites and attaches to a hiker's skin in the woods.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clinical medicine treats sick individuals, whereas public health protects entire populations by preventing disease and injury.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Public health focuses on treating individual patients in hospital emergency rooms after they become severely ill.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does tetanus require a deep puncture wound rather than a shallow surface scrape to produce dangerous bacterial toxins?
What biological difference separates how a person contracts Lyme disease or West Nile virus from how COVID-19 spreads?
Under what food storage conditions does Clostridium botulinum multiply and release neurotoxins inside sealed containers?
Which protective gear and removal tool should you carry on a hike to prevent blacklegged ticks from transmitting Borrelia?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Injectable inactivated flu vaccines contain only killed viral proteins that cannot replicate, though mild immune soreness is normal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inactivated flu shots contain live influenza viruses that regularly give healthy recipients a mild case of the flu.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Immunity to tetanus and diphtheria wanes over time, so adults require a Tdap or Td booster dose once every ten years.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Childhood vaccinations provide permanent lifetime immunity against every pathogen without requiring adult booster doses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Injecting donor antibodies is passive immunity, whereas active immunization trains your own B cells and T cells to build memory.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Active immunization works by injecting pre-made donor antibodies that immediately neutralize bacteria in the bloodstream.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tetanus and COVID-19 have routine human vaccines, but E. coli, salmonellosis, AIDS, and Lyme disease currently lack routine shots.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard childhood vaccines protect campers against all seven diseases listed in Public Health requirement 1b.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens inside the adaptive immune system after a vaccine introduces a weakened or inactivated antigen into the body?
Why must adults receive a tetanus and diphtheria booster every 10 years while an influenza vaccine is needed every year?
What immunization record details must a Scout verify on the Annual Health and Medical Record before attending summer camp?
Which biological obstacles have prevented scientists from creating an effective human vaccine for HIV or Lyme disease?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wild mammals contaminate high-altitude streams with Giardia and Cryptosporidium cysts, so all backcountry water needs treatment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Clear, cold mountain stream water flowing far above timberline is free of waterborne pathogens and safe to drink untreated.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bringing water to a full rolling boil for one minute kills waterborne pathogens, though high elevations require up to three minutes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Backcountry water must be kept at a rolling boil for ten full minutes at sea level to kill bacteria, viruses, and cysts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Microfilters remove bacteria and protozoan cysts, but tiny viruses pass through unless you add chemical treatment or UV light.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard 0.2-micron hollow-fiber camp water filters physically trap all waterborne viruses alongside bacteria and protozoa.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Damp cloth towels harbor and transfer bacteria across every dish, so sanitized camp utensils must air-dry in a clean mesh bag.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wiping camp plates dry with a clean cotton towel right after the sanitizing dip keeps utensils cleaner than air-drying.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to chemical treatment contact time if backcountry stream water is icy cold and cloudy with sediment?
Which protozoan cysts survive standard chlorine tablets but are killed by a full rolling boil or removed by a microfilter?
What water temperature or chemical concentration confirms that the third camp dishwashing pot actually sanitizes utensils?
Why is it dangerous to dry sanitized camp dishes with a shared cloth dishtowel instead of letting them air-dry in a mesh bag?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dry sweeping launches hantavirus particles into the air, so you must soak rodent droppings with bleach solution and wipe with paper.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sweeping up dried mouse droppings with a broom and dustpan is the safest way to clean a rodent-infested camp cabin.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dryer sheets fail to stop biting vectors; effective protection requires DEET, picaridin, or permethrin-treated clothing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hanging scented dryer sheets from your belt loops repels mosquitoes and ticks just as effectively as EPA-registered DEET.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mosquitoes fly across property lines from wetlands and storm drains, so community-wide larviciding and drainage are required.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Individual homeowners can eliminate regional mosquito-borne disease outbreaks simply by spraying their own backyards.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rodents smell food through plastic and chew straight through tent fabric, so all camp food belongs in hard animal-proof containers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving sealed plastic bags of food inside a nylon tent overnight prevents mice and rats from entering your sleeping area.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a mechanical vector like a housefly from a biological vector like an Anopheles mosquito or deer tick?
Where around a campsite or backyard can stagnant water collect and let Aedes mosquitoes complete their larval life cycle?
Why is it dangerous to dry-sweep rodent droppings inside an enclosed camp cabin instead of wetting them with disinfectant?
Which vector control tasks can one household accomplish alone, and which require a municipal abatement district to manage?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Primary treatment only settles solids; biological microbes in secondary treatment and disinfection are needed to make effluent safe.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Primary wastewater settling tanks remove dissolved organic pollutants and waterborne bacteria before water enters a river.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sanitary landfills seal waste daily over clay and synthetic liners while pipes collect liquid leachate and methane gas safely.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern municipal landfills are unlined pits designed to expose buried garbage to air and sunlight for rapid composting.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus produce heat-stable toxins in the 40 to 140 degree F danger zone that cooking cannot destroy.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Reheating spoiled food that sat on a warm counter for six hours makes it safe to eat because heat kills all bacteria.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Contaminated gloves spread pathogens just like bare skin, so workers must wash hands thoroughly before putting on fresh gloves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing disposable latex or nitrile gloves in a commercial kitchen eliminates the need for workers to wash their hands.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens during secondary wastewater treatment that primary physical screening and settling tanks cannot accomplish?
What internal and holding temperatures confirm that a cafeteria keeps perishable foods out of the bacterial danger zone?
Which engineering barriers inside a modern sanitary landfill prevent toxic leachate from seeping into local groundwater?
Where should a food service worker store raw poultry inside a walk-in cooler so meat juices never contaminate salad greens?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vape aerosols contain high-dose nicotine, heavy metals, and ultrafine chemical particles that injure developing lungs and brains.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Electronic cigarettes and vape pens emit harmless water vapor free of addictive chemicals or lung-damaging toxins.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prescription drugs are dosed for one patient's physiology and can cause fatal respiratory depression or heart failure in others.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prescription painkillers and stimulants are safe to share with friends because a licensed doctor originally prescribed them.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mammalian cochlear hair cells do not grow back once destroyed by excessive decibels, making noise-induced hearing loss permanent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inner ear sensory hair cells damaged by loud concerts, power tools, or gunfire regenerate within a few days of quiet rest.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only the liver metabolizes alcohol at a fixed rate over time; caffeine and cold water cannot lower blood alcohol concentration.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinking black coffee or taking a cold shower sobers up an intoxicated person by speeding alcohol removal from the blood.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the delicate hair cells inside the cochlea after repeated exposure to noise levels above 85 decibels?
Why does fine particulate matter (PM2.5) pose a deeper respiratory and cardiovascular threat than coarse dust particles?
Under what physiological mechanism does taking someone else's prescription opioid suppress breathing in the brainstem?
Which Air Quality Index (AQI) reading signals that your patrol should modify or postpone strenuous outdoor hiking?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mortality measures the incidence of death in a population, whereas morbidity measures the prevalence or incidence of illness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Morbidity and mortality are interchangeable medical terms that both measure how many people die from a disease each year.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High-morbidity conditions like respiratory infections sicken thousands, while heart disease and cancer cause the most deaths.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The four leading causes of illness in a county are always identical to the four leading causes of death in that community.

extra_misconceptions.fact: City, county, and state health departments hold primary legal authority locally, and the CDC assists when requested or interstate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Federal agencies like the CDC automatically take command of every local restaurant inspection and county health clinic.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Mandatory disease reporting and vital statistics let health agencies spot clusters early and intervene before outbreaks escalate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Public health departments wait until hospitals overflow before tracking infectious diseases or chronic illness trends.

extra_socratic_questions: What epidemiological distinction separates a community's leading causes of mortality from its leading causes of morbidity?
Why do epidemiologists calculate age-adjusted rates per 100,000 residents instead of comparing raw death counts across counties?
What surveillance data and laboratory reports trigger a county health department to launch an outbreak investigation?
Which local, state, and federal public health agencies coordinate resources when a foodborne or viral outbreak crosses borders?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Public health relies on non-clinical specialists including biostatisticians, sanitarians, health educators, and toxicologists.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in the public health sector requires graduating from medical school or holding a clinical nursing license.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Microbiologists run lab assays, whereas epidemiologists analyze population data, interview patients, and design field studies.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Epidemiologists spend their entire careers working alone at laboratory microscopes identifying bacteria and viruses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Environmental health specialists test emergency drinking water, assess shelter sanitation, and control vectors after disasters.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Registered Environmental Health Specialists only inspect restaurant kitchens and have no role in emergency disasters.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Biostatisticians design sampling methods before studies begin and build mathematical models to forecast disease transmission.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Biostatisticians only tally simple spreadsheet totals after a clinical study or public health campaign has already ended.

extra_socratic_questions: What academic coursework and field practicum experience distinguish a Master of Public Health (MPH) from a medical degree?
Which state or national credentialing exam must an environmental health specialist pass to conduct official inspections?
What statistical software and field interview logs does an applied epidemiologist maintain during a contact-tracing surge?
What personal protective equipment and biosafety training must a public health laboratory microbiologist verify daily?
